rv.q: This is breathtaking theatre with its own arresting imagination.
Standing ovations are ten a penny these days but this show thoroughly deserves the one it gets.

They're in search of a more visceral, live hit of the show's successful comedy-horror-sci-fi combination, and that's what director Stephen Daldry's eye-widening, often heart-racing production delivers.
The real spectacle here is that of a franchise eating itself.
The biggest frustration with it is the sense that it might have been show of the year with 30 minutes of really ruthless cuts.
Amid all the crowd scenes there's little sense of depth to the individual characters or how they relate to one another.
This astounding show definitely feels like a new chapter in theatre.
The writing is wonky but oh the dash, the drive, the grab of the staging.

Whether you are a die-hard fan poring over how this fits into the Stranger Things canon, or a Hawkins newbie feeling a little confused, The First Shadow is so mesmerising it is impossible not to be stunned by the spectacle of this electrifying show.

But for Stranger Things fans, this periodic schlockiness is all part of the show’s knowingly retro charm – and its old-school, bombastic thrills should get brand new audiences flocking to the West End.
But it is an extraordinary, gripping spectacle.
The result is a success in its own right.
This shiny three-hour-long transplant looks every penny of its eye-watering cost.
These are only a few of the incredible people made this production possible; it has taken a massive team to make it genuinely magical, mind-blowing, and thrilling.
Fans of the Netflix show will feel right at home here, as the world of Hawkins, Indiana is recreated beautifully on the stage.
Director Stephen Daldry summons all of his theatrical and film-making powers like a latter day Prospero.

Without a doubt, this is one of the most major and quality productions of the year, and while many of the occurrences in the story may seem strange, its triumphant success won’t be the strangest thing.
This is formidable, engaging theatre that is in productive dialogue with the resources of the screen, both narrative and formal.
Sometimes it seems there is an information overload, but every moment grabs your attention as you try to sort out what is going on.
The First Shadow is a show that simultaneously hits and misses.
It's not bad, but I drifted off on occasion, and still managed to easily follow proceedings.
